task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: opponent next-possession PPP after play type
methodological_questions: measurement of opponent points per possession after a specific play type
threshold determination for an AVOID label
sample size per play type and by success/failure
confounding by game situation and opponent quality
reliability and validity of play-type labels
handling of end-of-possession events (fouls, dead balls)

historical_evidence.finding: Sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock found: after the opponent runs a successful play type X, opponent next-possession PPP is reduced by 0.119 to 0.135 PPP across all 8 play types, replicated in playoffs. Own-next PPP baseline is 0.975 (n=18,943), but own-sequence effects were exploratory. Top pair premiums identified.

Play-type labeling audit: OTHER possessions had 36% foul endings, inflating PPP; DRIVE showed 12 pp below foul benchmark; only 0.7% of possessions map to a play type via initiation_type. Play-type PPP differences are, in part, labeling artifacts rather than real efficiency.

failed_approaches.what_failed: interpreting play-type PPP differences as real efficiency without accounting for labelling artifacts
failed_approaches.why: OTHER PPP inflated by foul endings, DRIVE foul leakage, and near-zero mapping of initiation_type to play type

evidence_establishes: After a successful offensive play type, opponent next-possession PPP drops by 0.12–0.14 relative to a baseline of 1.206; this defensive aftershock is consistent across all 8 play types and replicates in playoffs.
Own-next possession baseline is 0.975 PPP, but own-sequence lag effects were not fully characterized and were treated as exploratory.
Play-type classification contains substantial artifacts: foul leakage inflates OTHER and depresses DRIVE relative to foul benchmarks, and the initiation_type field fails to map most possessions.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the observed defensive aftershock is large enough to drive an AVOID label, because no label threshold is defined.
Whether the aftershock differs between successful and unsuccessful play types, or is a generic dead-ball/score effect rather than play-type-specific disruption.
The magnitude and direction of own-sequence lag effects for each play type.
That play-type labels are sufficiently reliable for sequencing-based labeling decisions; the labeling audit suggests otherwise.
How team- or context-specific the effects are, given small team-level cell sizes.
own_inferences: An AVOID label would require an operational threshold (e.g., opponent PPP above a certain value or a net negative effect); without it the question is ill‑posed.

Because the known aftershock is beneficial (opponent scores less), an AVOID label might target play types that fail to produce this benefit or that occur after unsuccessful plays, requiring stratification by play outcome.
Labeling artifacts are severe enough that any naive analysis of play-type PPP sequences risks producing an artifact-driven conclusion.
A valid test would need to first validate play-type assignments, then condition on game state and outcome, and apply a pre-registered threshold.
uncertainties: The exact magnitude of opponent next‑possession PPP after each play type, overall and by success/failure, across different game states.
Whether the defensive aftershock is causal or a spurious artefact of foul structuring and dead-ball patterns.
The reliability of the derived play-type possession records in [source] database, given the low initiation_type mapping rate.
The appropriate threshold for an AVOID label—both statistical and practical—has not been established.
Own-sequence lag effects are underpowered and have not been validated.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical evidence changed the decision from an initial presumption of testability to a recommendation not to proceed. [prior work] already shows a robust defensive aftershock (beneficial) after successful plays, which undermines a simple AVOID narrative. SF-[prior work] reveals labelling artifacts that would likely dominate any attempt to measure marginal differences across play types. Together they suggest that the question as posed—without a precise threshold and with current label quality—would produce a misleading or artifactual result.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labels contain severe artefactual biases (foul leakage, poor initiation_type mapping) that undermine the foundation of the analysis.
The AVOID label threshold is undefined; a decision rule must be supplied to make the question testable.
Some play types have low per-game frequency and even lower counts when stratified by success/failure and game context.
Opponent quality, game score, time remaining, and dead-ball frequency are plausible confounders that must be controlled.
Comparing multiple play types (and possibly their interactions) inflates false-positive risk unless multiplicity is controlled.

prior_work.summary: [prior work] established that successful play types produce a large and consistent defensive aftershock, but left own‑sequence lags as exploratory. SF-[prior work] showed that play‑type PPPs are artefactually distorted. Neither study addressed an explicit AVOID labelling threshold.

risks.text: Play‑type labels from [source] database have documented artefactual foul leakage and near‑zero initiation‑type mapping; any effect size estimate may reflect label error rather than true defensive quality.
AVOID labels require a subjective threshold; without a pre‑registered definition, the analysis is susceptible to cherry‑picking and hindsight bias.
Play types such as PUTBACK or CUT have relatively small sample sizes, especially after splitting by success/failure and opponent context, limiting statistical power.
Game situation (score, period, shot clock), opponent defensive strategy, and dead‑ball frequency may confound the relationship between a play type and the next possession PPP.
Testing 8+ play types and possibly multiple lags inflates the risk of false positives unless a correction is applied.
Despite large overall possession counts, power to detect small but practically important differences in own‑sequence lags or differential aftershock may be inadequate without careful aggregation.
The underlying play‑type labels are produced by an imperfect classification system; label noise will attenuate any true sequential effects toward zero.

design.estimand: The difference between opponent next-possession PPP after play type X (unconditional on success) and a league-average opponent-possession PPP baseline, together with the own-team next-possession PPP difference. A play type receives an AVOID label if the estimated opponent PPP difference exceeds +0.05 and the own-team PPP difference is less than -0.02, both statistically significant after multiplicity adjustment, or a pre-registered composite cost score surpasses a threshold.
design.unit: A tagged play-type possession, with a valid play‑type label from a cleaned and validated classification (exclude OTHER and possessions with high foul-ending probability unless properly adjusted), followed by a successful defensive/offensive possession (no immediate dead ball, end of period, or substitution that breaks the link).
design.sample: All NBA regular-season and playoff games from 2022-23 through 2025-26, excluding possessions where the next possession cannot be reliably assigned (e.g., end of quarter, immediate fouls that lead to free throws without a change of possession). The analysis would use a minimum of 2000 such linked pairs per play type per season to ensure power.
design.power: Power analysis: assuming an effect size of 0.04 PPP and residual standard deviation of 0.35 PPP, at least 2,500 linked possessions per play type per comparison are needed for 80% power at α=0.05 (two-sided) with Bonferroni correction for 8 play types. Total available sample from multiple seasons exceeds this for most play types, but sparse types (PUTBACK, CUT) may require pooling across seasons.
design.controls: Control for game score differential, period, possession clock, opponent defensive rating (prior season or current season), home/away, and whether the preceding possession ended with a made shot, defensive rebound, or dead-ball turnover. Use fixed effects for team and season.
design.falsification: Falsification test 1: Shuffle play-type labels randomly within each game to verify that the observed AVOID thresholds disappear. Falsification test 2: Compare the proposed label threshold to a ‘placebo’ threshold defined on the same data but using a holdout season not used for estimation. Falsification test 3: Confirm that labelling decisions are not driven by the most common context (e.g., late-game fouling) by excluding last two minutes of each half and seeing if labels remain stable.
design.multiplicity: Use the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure across all 8 play types for both opponent and own PPP comparisons (16 tests); a play type is assigned an AVOID label only if the adjusted p-value remains below 0.05 and the effect size exceeds the pre-registered thresholds.
design.decision_rule: A play type X is labelled AVOID if, after multiplicity adjustment, opponent next-possession PPP increases by more than 0.05 (95% CI does not include 0) and own-team next-possession PPP does not increase by more than 0.02; the union of these rules must replicate in a holdout set of the most recent full season (2025-26) not used for discovery.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, substitution, starter, and box-score data for 2022-23 through 2025-26, processed through a validated play-by-play parser to produce the possession graph, with play-type labels corrected for foul leakage per SF-[prior work] methodology.
